answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so a node’s influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than identity claims alone. A sybil cluster—whether labeled pigment, reef, or raven—can accumulate little external connectivity; its sparse boundary gives low conductance, limiting walk escape and mixing. Thus min-cut and transitivity bounds constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight to its incoming trusted support plus bounded leakage, not its raw identity count.
